result.title: Complex materials engineering via Provenance Action Graphs: potential, structure and demonstration
result.summary: This work discusses and tests the potential of reaction graphs for material synthesis, in which events consist of reaction steps (actions) and their outputs (observations). The importance comes from the requirement to synthesize technologically useful materials, especially those that are kinetically stabilized. Often, it is a science that follows years of trial and error, culminating in (published) successful recipes, but is truly driven by far more (unpublished) failures. The entry into the era of AI provides an opportunity to use learning algorithms to encode rules from multi-dimensional synthesis pathways, regardless of their technological usefulness, and to decode both forward prediction and inverse learning modes. The main incentive is to accelerate material discovery by generating a global knowledge base that can be shared among data agents and contributed to by them. We will focus on several scenarios in the common synthesis process during solid-state synthesis, primarily because these reactions are kinetic in nature and require closer monitoring and control of the reaction history.

AI.brief_summary: 论文讨论并测试用 provenance action graph（反应图）表示材料合成过程，其中事件由反应步骤（动作）及其产物（观测）组成，并探讨学习算法从多维合成路径中编码规则、支持前向预测与逆向学习的潜力，目标是建立可共享的合成知识库以加速材料发现。
AI.relevance_reason: 材料合成属较远领域，但「动作—观测」事件图与路径知识库的组织方式，可能与 LVR 中推理轨迹表示、前向/逆向状态预测及轨迹复用与监督分配存在概念联系，可供核查。
